tools.name: search_tools
tools.description: Search the registry's OSINT tools by words, the input type they take, the entity type they find, or category. passive_only keeps the tools ot runs without asking the person.

tools.name: get_tool
tools.description: A tool's inputs, outputs, API keys, network access and ethics flags, the consent class `ot mcp` will put a run in, what a run does in plain words, and how to install and run it with ot.

tools.name: list_types
tools.description: The input types tools take, the entity types they find, the categories, and which input types each entity type can feed (the pivot map).

tools.name: suggest_pivots
tools.description: For entity types found so far (a subdomain, an account, an email ...), the tools that take them as input, best first.

tools.name: search_guides
tools.description: Search the registry's investigation guides (methods, checklists, references) by words, target type or level.

tools.name: read_guide
tools.description: One page of a guide, as Markdown, with the list of its pages and the tools it uses.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_types · Private data: get_tool · Public sink: suggest_pivots · Destructive: get_tool.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_types · Private data: get_tool · Public sink: suggest_pivots · Destructive: get_tool

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
